items.name: Barbell Curl
items.summary: The staple biceps builder: stand tall and curl a straight bar from your thighs to your shoulders.

items.name: EZ-Bar Curl
items.summary: A barbell curl on the angled EZ-bar, which puts the wrists in a more comfortable semi-supinated position.

items.name: Drag Curl
items.summary: A barbell curl where you drag the bar up your body with the elbows travelling back, which takes the front delts out and keeps tension on the biceps.

items.name: EZ-Bar Preacher Curl
items.summary: A strict curl with your upper arms braced on a preacher bench, which stops any swinging and works the biceps hard in the stretched position.

items.name: Dumbbell Curl
items.summary: Curl a pair of dumbbells, together or alternating, turning the palms up as they rise.

items.name: Hammer Curl
items.summary: A dumbbell curl with a neutral, thumbs-up grip that shifts the work toward the brachialis and brachioradialis.

items.name: Cross-Body Hammer Curl
items.summary: A hammer curl where each dumbbell travels across your body toward the opposite shoulder, hitting the brachialis and brachioradialis hard.

items.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
items.summary: Curls lying back on an incline bench so your arms hang behind your body, loading the biceps in a deep stretch.

items.name: Concentration Curl
items.summary: A seated one-arm curl with your elbow braced against your inner thigh, making it nearly impossible to cheat.

items.name: Spider Curl
items.summary: Curls lying chest-down on an incline bench with your arms hanging straight down, which keeps tension on the biceps at the top of the rep.

items.name: Zottman Curl
items.summary: Curl up with palms up, rotate to palms down at the top, then lower slowly overhand: biceps on the way up, forearms on the way down.

items.name: Dumbbell Preacher Curl
items.summary: A one-arm preacher curl with a dumbbell, letting you train each arm on its own with the upper arm braced.

items.name: Cable Curl
items.summary: A standing curl on a low pulley with a straight or EZ handle, which keeps steady tension on the biceps through the whole rep.

items.name: Rope Hammer Curl
items.summary: A hammer curl on a low pulley with a rope, working the brachialis and brachioradialis with constant cable tension.

items.name: Bayesian Cable Curl
items.summary: A one-arm curl facing away from a low pulley so the cable pulls your arm behind you, loading the biceps in a long stretch.

items.name: Overhead Cable Curl
items.summary: Curls with both arms held out to the sides at shoulder height between two high pulleys, like a front double-biceps pose.

items.name: Machine Preacher Curl
items.summary: A preacher curl on a selectorised or plate-loaded machine, which fixes the path so you can push close to failure safely.

items.name: Band Curl
items.summary: Curls with a resistance band anchored under your feet; the band gets harder as you near the top.

items.name: Suspension Trainer Biceps Curl
items.summary: A bodyweight curl on a suspension trainer such as a TRX: lean back and curl your body toward your hands.

items.name: Triceps Pushdown
items.summary: The go-to triceps exercise: push a straight or V-bar down on a high pulley until your arms are straight.

items.name: Rope Pushdown
items.summary: A triceps pushdown with a rope, spreading the ends apart at the bottom for a harder lockout.

items.name: Single-Arm Cable Pushdown
items.summary: A one-arm pushdown with a D-handle on a high pulley, letting you train each side on its own.

items.name: Reverse-Grip Pushdown
items.summary: A pushdown with an underhand grip on a straight or EZ bar, which makes it harder to cheat with the shoulders.

items.name: Band Pushdown
items.summary: A triceps pushdown with a resistance band anchored overhead, good for home workouts and warm-ups.

items.name: Overhead Cable Triceps Extension
items.summary: Face away from a cable and extend a rope overhead, training the triceps' long head in a deep stretch.

items.name: Single-Arm Cable Overhead Extension
items.summary: A one-arm overhead extension on a cable, letting you stretch and train each triceps on its own.

items.name: Dumbbell Overhead Extension
items.summary: Hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands and lower it behind your head, stretching the triceps' long head.

items.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Overhead Extension
items.summary: A one-arm overhead extension with a light dumbbell, lowering it behind your head and pressing it back up.

items.name: EZ-Bar Overhead Extension
items.summary: A seated overhead triceps extension with an EZ-bar, allowing heavier loading than a single dumbbell.

items.name: Band Overhead Triceps Extension
items.summary: An overhead triceps extension with a resistance band anchored under your foot or low behind you.

items.name: Skull Crusher
items.summary: A lying triceps extension: on a flat bench, lower an EZ-bar toward your forehead by bending the elbows, then extend.

items.name: Dumbbell Skull Crusher
items.summary: A lying triceps extension with a dumbbell in each hand and palms facing in, often easier on the wrists and elbows than a bar.

items.name: Bodyweight Triceps Extension
items.summary: A bodyweight skull crusher: lean onto a bar or bench edge and bend at the elbows to lower your head below your hands.

items.name: Close-Grip Bench Press
items.summary: A bench press with hands about shoulder-width and elbows tucked, shifting the work from the chest to the triceps.

items.name: JM Press
items.summary: A powerlifting hybrid of a close-grip bench press and a skull crusher, lowering the bar toward your chin with the elbows forward.

items.name: Tate Press
items.summary: A lying dumbbell triceps extension where the elbows flare out and the dumbbells lower to touch your chest.

items.name: Dumbbell Triceps Kickback
items.summary: Hinge forward with your upper arm parallel to the floor and straighten your elbow to kick a dumbbell back.

items.name: Cable Triceps Kickback
items.summary: A triceps kickback on a low pulley, which keeps tension on the muscle at full lockout where dumbbells go light.

items.name: Machine Triceps Extension
items.summary: A seated triceps extension machine with the upper arms braced on a pad, an easy way to load the triceps safely.

items.name: Seated Dip Machine
items.summary: A seated machine that mimics a dip, pressing handles down beside your hips.

items.name: Triceps Dip
items.summary: A dip on parallel bars with an upright torso and elbows tucked, keeping the emphasis on the triceps rather than the chest.

items.name: Bench Dip
items.summary: A dip with your hands on a bench behind you and your feet on the floor, an easy entry point to triceps dips.

items.name: Diamond Push-Up
items.summary: A push-up with your hands together under your chest, thumbs and index fingers forming a diamond, to load the triceps.

items.name: Dumbbell Wrist Curl
items.summary: With your forearms resting on your thighs or a bench, curl dumbbells up using only your wrists to train the forearm flexors.

items.name: Barbell Wrist Curl
items.summary: A wrist curl with a barbell held in both hands, forearms resting on a bench, for heavier forearm flexor work.

items.name: Reverse Wrist Curl
items.summary: A wrist curl with palms facing down, lifting the back of the hands to train the forearm extensors.

items.name: Behind-the-Back Wrist Curl
items.summary: Standing with a barbell held behind you, curl it up with your wrists, letting you go heavier than seated wrist curls.

items.name: Barbell Finger Curl
items.summary: Let a barbell roll down to your fingertips and curl it back into your palm, training the finger flexors for crushing grip.

items.name: Reverse Curl
items.summary: A curl with an overhand grip, which shifts the load onto the brachioradialis and forearm extensors.

items.name: Dumbbell Reverse Curl
items.summary: An overhand curl with dumbbells, working the brachioradialis and forearm extensors one or both arms at a time.

items.name: Radial Deviation
items.summary: Lift the head of a hammer, or a dumbbell loaded at one end, by tilting your wrist toward your thumb; good for wrist health and grip.

items.name: Ulnar Deviation
items.summary: Lift the head of a hammer, or a dumbbell loaded at one end, behind you by tilting your wrist toward your little finger.

items.name: Hammer Pronation and Supination
items.summary: Rotate a hammer, or a dumbbell loaded at one end, palm down and palm up to strengthen the forearm rotators; a staple for elbow and wrist health.

items.name: Wrist Roller
items.summary: Roll a weight up on a cord by twisting a handle with your wrists, then lower it back down; brutal for the whole forearm.

items.name: Plate Pinch
items.summary: Pinch two smooth weight plates together between your fingers and thumb and hold them for time, building pinch grip.

items.name: Hand Gripper
items.summary: Squeeze a spring-loaded hand gripper shut to build crushing grip strength.

items.name: Band Finger Extension
items.summary: Spread your fingers against a small rubber band to train the finger extensors, balancing grip work and helping the elbows.

items.name: Fat-Grip Dumbbell Hold
items.summary: Hold heavy dumbbells with thick grip attachments (such as Fat Gripz) for time, building open-hand grip strength.

items.name: Towel Hang
items.summary: Hang from two towels draped over a pull-up bar for time, a tough test of grip that carries over to climbing and grappling.

items.name: Pull-Up
items.summary: The benchmark bodyweight pull for the lats: hang from a bar with an overhand grip and pull your chest up to it.

items.name: Chin-Up
items.summary: A pull-up with an underhand, shoulder-width grip, which brings the biceps in more and is usually a little easier.

items.name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
items.summary: A pull-up on parallel handles with palms facing each other, often the most shoulder- and elbow-friendly grip.

items.name: Wide-Grip Pull-Up
items.summary: A pull-up with a grip well outside the shoulders, which shortens the range and biases the lats and upper back.

items.name: Weighted Pull-Up
items.summary: A pull-up with extra load from a dip belt, weight vest or a dumbbell between the feet, for building strength past bodyweight.

items.name: Assisted Pull-Up Machine
items.summary: A pull-up on a machine whose knee or foot pad pushes you up, so you can train the full movement while building up to bodyweight.

items.name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up
items.summary: A pull-up with a long resistance band looped over the bar and under your knee or foot to take off some of your bodyweight.

items.name: Negative Pull-Up
items.summary: A slow lowering from the top of a pull-up, used to build the strength for your first full reps.

items.name: L-Sit Pull-Up
items.summary: A strict pull-up with the legs held straight out in front at hip height, which adds a hard hip flexor and ab hold.

items.name: Archer Pull-Up
items.summary: A wide-grip pull-up toward one hand while the other arm straightens along the bar, a step toward one-arm pull-ups.

items.name: Typewriter Pull-Up
items.summary: A wide-grip pull-up where you slide from one hand to the other at the top, keeping your chin at bar height.

items.name: Scapular Pull-Up
items.summary: Small pulls from a dead hang using only the shoulder blades, to teach the start of a pull-up and strengthen the lower traps and lats.

items.name: Dead Hang
items.summary: Hanging from a bar with straight arms and relaxed shoulders, mainly a grip builder that also decompresses and opens the shoulders.

items.name: Active Hang
items.summary: A hang with the shoulder blades pulled down and the arms straight, training the shoulder position every pull-up starts from.

items.name: Bar Muscle-Up
items.summary: An explosive pull that carries your body over the bar, then a dip to lockout on top.

items.name: Ring Muscle-Up
items.summary: A muscle-up on gymnastic rings: a false-grip pull, a deep transition and a ring dip to support on top.

items.name: Tuck Front Lever
items.summary: The first front lever progression: hang under the bar with straight arms and hold your back level with the floor, knees tucked to the chest.

items.name: Advanced Tuck Front Lever
items.summary: A tuck front lever with a flat back and the hips opened to 90°, which makes the lever noticeably longer and harder.

items.name: Straddle Front Lever
items.summary: A front lever with straight legs spread wide, the step before the full lever.

items.name: Front Lever
items.summary: Holding your whole body straight and horizontal, face up, beneath a bar with straight arms: a top-tier lat and core strength skill.

items.name: Tuck Back Lever
items.summary: The first back lever progression: hang face down beneath a bar or rings with straight arms and your knees tucked.

items.name: Back Lever
items.summary: Holding your body straight and horizontal, face down, beneath a bar or rings with your arms straight behind you.

items.name: Lat Pulldown
items.summary: The cable machine version of a pull-up: pull a wide bar from overhead down to your upper chest.

items.name: Close-Grip Lat Pulldown
items.summary: A pulldown with a close, neutral V-handle, which gives a longer range of motion and a strong lat contraction.

items.name: Underhand Lat Pulldown
items.summary: A pulldown with a shoulder-width, palms-up grip, the cable version of a chin-up with more biceps involvement.

items.name: Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
items.summary: A one-arm pulldown with a D-handle on a high cable, for evening out sides and getting a deep lat stretch.

items.name: Machine Lat Pulldown
items.summary: A pulldown on a plate-loaded or selectorised machine with fixed handles, often with independent arms.

items.name: Band Lat Pulldown
items.summary: A pulldown with a resistance band anchored overhead, for training the lats at home or as a warm-up.

items.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
items.summary: A lat isolation exercise: with arms nearly straight, sweep a cable bar or rope from overhead down to your thighs.

items.name: Band Straight-Arm Pulldown
items.summary: The straight-arm pulldown with a band anchored high, a handy lat activation drill before pull-ups.

items.name: Cable Lat Prayer
items.summary: A kneeling straight-arm pulldown with the hands together on a rope, hinging forward to get a deep lat stretch and contraction.

items.name: Pullover Machine
items.summary: A machine that isolates the lats by rotating your arms from overhead down to your torso against a pad.

items.name: Barbell Row
items.summary: The classic bent-over row: hinge forward with a flat back and row a barbell to your lower ribs.

items.name: Pendlay Row
items.summary: A strict barbell row from a dead stop on the floor each rep, with the torso parallel to the ground.

items.name: Yates Row
items.summary: An underhand barbell row with a more upright torso, rowing to the waist so you can use heavy weight with less lower back strain.

items.name: Seal Row
items.summary: A barbell row lying face down on a high bench, which removes all momentum and lower back load.

items.name: T-Bar Row
items.summary: A row with one end of a barbell anchored in a landmine or corner, pulling a V-handle under the chest.

items.name: Meadows Row
items.summary: A one-arm landmine row standing side-on to the bar and gripping its thick end, named after John Meadows.

items.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
items.summary: A single-arm dumbbell row with one hand and knee on a bench, rowing the weight toward your hip.

items.name: Bent-Over Dumbbell Row
items.summary: A two-arm bent-over row with dumbbells, which lets each arm move freely and the wrists find a neutral position.

items.name: Kroc Row
items.summary: A heavy, high-rep one-arm dumbbell row with a little controlled body English, built for back size and grip strength.

items.name: Incline Dumbbell Row
items.summary: A chest-supported dumbbell row face down on an incline bench, taking the lower back out of it.

items.name: Kettlebell Row
items.summary: A single-arm bent-over row with a kettlebell, supported on a bench or your knee.

items.name: Kettlebell Gorilla Row
items.summary: Alternating rows from a deep, wide hinge with two kettlebells on the floor, pressing into one while rowing the other.

items.name: Seated Cable Row
items.summary: A seated row on a low cable with a close V-handle, pulling to your stomach and squeezing the shoulder blades together.

items.name: Wide-Grip Cable Row
items.summary: A seated cable row with a wide overhand bar, rowing to the lower chest to bias the upper back and rear delts.

items.name: Single-Arm Cable Row
items.summary: A one-arm cable row with a D-handle, seated or standing, for a longer range and even work on both sides.

items.name: Chest-Supported Machine Row
items.summary: A row on a machine with a chest pad, plate-loaded or selectorised, so you can push hard without any lower back load.

items.name: Machine High Row
items.summary: A plate-loaded row where the handles start high in front and come down and back, between a pulldown and a row.

items.name: Inverted Row
items.summary: A horizontal bodyweight pull: hang under a bar set at waist height with a straight body and pull your chest up to it.

items.name: Ring Row
items.summary: An inverted row on gymnastic rings, which lets your hands rotate freely and adds a little stability work.

items.name: TRX Row
items.summary: A bodyweight row on a suspension trainer, adjusting difficulty by how far you lean back.

items.name: Band Row
items.summary: A seated or standing row with a resistance band, anchored in front at chest height or looped around your feet.

items.name: Barbell Shrug
items.summary: The standard upper trap builder: hold a barbell at arm's length and shrug your shoulders straight up.

items.name: Dumbbell Shrug
items.summary: A shrug holding dumbbells at your sides, which lets your arms hang naturally and the shoulders move freely.

items.name: Trap Bar Shrug
items.summary: A shrug inside a trap (hex) bar, with the load at your sides for a natural shoulder line and heavy loading.

items.name: Behind-the-Back Barbell Shrug
items.summary: A barbell shrug holding the bar behind your thighs, which pulls the shoulders back slightly and shifts work toward the mid traps.

items.name: Smith Machine Shrug
items.summary: A barbell shrug on a Smith machine, with a fixed bar path so you can focus purely on the traps.

items.name: Cable Shrug
items.summary: A shrug with a bar or handles on a low cable, giving steady tension through the whole range.

items.name: Incline Dumbbell Shrug
items.summary: A shrug lying face down on an incline bench, pulling the shoulder blades up and together to target the mid traps.

items.name: Overhead Shrug
items.summary: A shrug with a barbell locked out overhead in a wide grip, training the upper traps in the position used for pressing and snatching.

items.name: Treadmill Run
items.summary: Running on a motorised treadmill at a steady pace or in intervals, a controllable way to build aerobic fitness.

items.name: Incline Treadmill Walk
items.summary: Brisk walking on a steep treadmill incline, a low-impact way to raise your heart rate and work the glutes and calves.

items.name: Curved Treadmill Run
items.summary: Running on a self-powered curved treadmill, where your own stride drives the belt; great for sprints and harder than a motorised belt at the same pace.

items.name: Rowing Machine
items.summary: Full-body cardio on an indoor rower; most of the power comes from the leg drive, finished by the hips leaning back and the arms pulling.

items.name: Stationary Bike
items.summary: Steady or interval cycling on an upright exercise bike, a low-impact way to build aerobic fitness.

items.name: Recumbent Bike
items.summary: Cycling in a reclined, backed seat with the pedals in front of you; easy on the back and joints and good for beginners and rehab.

items.name: Spin Bike
items.summary: Indoor cycling on a heavy-flywheel spin bike, with seated climbs, standing efforts and sprints as in a spin class.

items.name: Air Bike
items.summary: A fan bike (Assault Bike, Echo Bike) with moving handles, so your arms push and pull while your legs pedal; the harder you go, the harder it gets.

items.name: Ski Erg
items.summary: Cardio on a ski ergometer, pulling two handles down from overhead like a double-pole ski stroke, driven by the lats, triceps and a hip hinge.

items.name: Elliptical
items.summary: Low-impact cardio on an elliptical trainer, gliding your feet in an oval path while pushing and pulling the moving handles.

items.name: Stair Climber
items.summary: Climbing a revolving staircase at a steady pace, a demanding low-impact cardio that works the legs and glutes hard.

items.name: VersaClimber
items.summary: A vertical climbing machine where your arms and legs move in opposition, like climbing a ladder; intense full-body cardio with no impact.

items.name: Arm Bike
items.summary: Cardio on an upper-body ergometer, cranking the handles in circles with your arms; useful when you need to rest your legs.

items.name: Easy Run
items.summary: A relaxed, conversational-pace run that builds your aerobic base and makes up most of a runner's weekly distance.

items.name: Sprints
items.summary: Short all-out runs, usually 10–100 m, with full or partial rest between, to build speed, power and anaerobic fitness.

items.name: Hill Sprints
items.summary: Short, hard sprints up a moderate hill; the slope builds power and makes sprinting easier on the hamstrings.

items.name: Shuttle Runs
items.summary: Repeated sprints back and forth between two markers, usually 10–25 m apart, training speed, acceleration and turning.

items.name: Stair Sprints
items.summary: Running up a flight of stairs or stadium steps as fast as you can, then walking down to recover.

items.name: Brisk Walk
items.summary: Walking at a quick, purposeful pace that raises your heart rate; the simplest cardio there is.

items.name: Rucking
items.summary: Brisk walking with a weighted backpack (a ruck), which turns an ordinary walk into strength-endurance training.

items.name: Freestyle Swim
items.summary: Front crawl in a pool, a no-impact full-body cardio led by the lats and shoulders, with a steady flutter kick.

items.name: Outdoor Cycling
items.summary: Riding a road, gravel or mountain bike outdoors, a low-impact endurance cardio you can do for hours.

items.name: Jump Rope
items.summary: Basic two-foot bounce with a skipping rope; simple, portable cardio that builds coordination and springy ankles.

items.name: Boxer Skip
items.summary: Jump rope with a light shift of weight from foot to foot on each turn, the relaxed rhythm boxers use for long rounds.

items.name: High-Knee Jump Rope
items.summary: Running on the spot over the rope, driving one knee to hip height on each turn; a hard, fast conditioning drill.

items.name: Double-Unders
items.summary: Jump rope where the rope passes under your feet twice per jump, demanding fast wrists, timing and a slightly higher jump.

items.name: Burpee
items.summary: Squat down, jump your feet back to a plank, do a push-up, jump your feet in and jump up: a full-body conditioning staple.

items.name: Burpee Box Jump-Over
items.summary: A burpee beside a box followed by jumping onto or over it, then another burpee on the far side.

items.name: Squat Thrust
items.summary: The burpee without the push-up or the jump: squat, kick your feet back to a plank and jump them back in.

items.name: Sprawl
items.summary: The wrestler's takedown defence: drop your hands to the floor, shoot your legs back and drive your hips to the ground, then pop back up.

items.name: Mountain Climbers
items.summary: From a high plank, drive your knees towards your chest one after the other at a running pace.

items.name: Jumping Jacks
items.summary: Jump your feet out wide while swinging your arms overhead, then jump back in; a classic warm-up and conditioning move.

items.name: Star Jumps
items.summary: From a quarter squat, jump explosively and spread your arms and legs into a star shape in the air, then land back together.

items.name: High Knees
items.summary: Running on the spot, driving each knee up to hip height as fast as you can.

items.name: Butt Kicks
items.summary: Jogging on the spot or forwards while kicking your heels up towards your glutes; a common running warm-up drill.

items.name: Lateral Shuffle
items.summary: Quick side-to-side shuffling in a low athletic stance, a staple agility and conditioning drill for court and field sports.

items.name: Bear Crawl
items.summary: Crawling forwards on your hands and feet with your knees hovering just off the floor, working the shoulders and core.

items.name: Crab Walk
items.summary: Walking on your hands and feet facing upwards with your hips lifted, working the triceps, shoulders and glutes.

items.name: Battle Rope Alternating Waves
items.summary: Whipping the ends of a heavy battle rope up and down one arm after the other to make alternating waves, a hard shoulder-led conditioning drill.

items.name: Battle Rope Double Waves
items.summary: Both arms raising and lowering together to send matching waves down a battle rope.

items.name: Battle Rope Slams
items.summary: Lifting both ends of a battle rope overhead and slamming them into the floor as hard as you can.

items.name: Wall Ball
items.summary: A full squat holding a soft medicine ball, then driving up and throwing it to a target high on a wall, catching it into the next squat.

items.name: Medicine Ball Burpee
items.summary: A burpee with your hands on a medicine ball, finished by pressing the ball overhead as you stand or jump.

items.name: Sled Sprint
items.summary: Pushing a lightly loaded sled as fast as you can over 10–30 m, building acceleration and leg power with no lowering phase.

items.name: Shadow Boxing
items.summary: Throwing punch combinations and moving on your feet against an imaginary opponent, building conditioning, rhythm and technique.

items.name: Heavy Bag Rounds
items.summary: Timed rounds of punching combinations on a heavy bag, with wraps and gloves, for conditioning and power.

items.name: Agility Ladder Drills
items.summary: Quick footwork patterns through a flat agility ladder on the floor (one foot in each box, two feet in, in-and-out, lateral steps), training speed and coordination.

items.name: Bench Press
items.summary: The classic barbell press for chest, front delts and triceps, done lying on a flat bench.

items.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
items.summary: A flat bench press with two dumbbells, which allows a deeper stretch than a barbell and makes each side work on its own.

items.name: Smith Machine Bench Press
items.summary: A flat bench press on a Smith machine; the fixed bar path makes it easy to push hard safely without a spotter.

items.name: Machine Chest Press
items.summary: A seated, guided press that trains the chest with no balance demand, making it easy to learn and to push close to failure.

items.name: Barbell Floor Press
items.summary: A bench press done lying on the floor; the floor cuts the range short, taking strain off the shoulders and loading the lockout and triceps hard.

items.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
items.summary: A dumbbell press lying on the floor, a shoulder-friendly option that needs no bench and stresses the top half of the press.

items.name: Neutral-Grip Dumbbell Press
items.summary: A flat dumbbell press with palms facing each other, which keeps the elbows tucked and is often easier on the shoulders.

items.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Bench Press
items.summary: A flat bench press with one dumbbell at a time, which trains each side alone and makes your core fight to stop you rolling off the bench.

items.name: Dumbbell Squeeze Press
items.summary: A flat press with the dumbbells squeezed hard together the whole time, which keeps the chest working through the full rep. Also called a crush press.

items.name: Standing Cable Chest Press
items.summary: A standing press with two cables, which keeps tension on the chest through the whole range and makes your core stabilise you.

items.name: Band Chest Press
items.summary: A standing chest press against a resistance band anchored behind you, a simple home or travel option.

items.name: Landmine Chest Press
items.summary: A standing two-handed press of a barbell anchored in a landmine, which presses up and forward on an incline path that hits the upper chest.

items.name: Incline Bench Press
items.summary: A barbell press on a 30–45° bench, shifting the work toward the upper chest and front delts.

items.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
items.summary: A dumbbell press on a 30–45° bench for the upper chest, with a deeper stretch than the barbell version.

items.name: Incline Smith Machine Press
items.summary: An incline press on a Smith machine, a stable way to load the upper chest without a spotter.

items.name: Incline Machine Press
items.summary: A seated machine press that pushes up and forward on an incline path to target the upper chest.

items.name: Decline Bench Press
items.summary: A barbell press on a bench angled head-down, which emphasises the lower chest and usually allows heavy loads with less shoulder stress.

items.name: Decline Dumbbell Press
items.summary: A dumbbell press on a decline bench for the lower chest, with each arm working on its own.

items.name: Dumbbell Fly
items.summary: A flat bench fly that stretches and squeezes the chest by opening and closing the arms in a wide arc.

items.name: Incline Dumbbell Fly
items.summary: A dumbbell fly on a 30–45° bench that focuses on the upper chest.

items.name: Decline Dumbbell Fly
items.summary: A dumbbell fly on a decline bench, which shifts the emphasis toward the lower chest.

items.name: Cable Fly
items.summary: A standing fly between two cables set at shoulder height, keeping constant tension on the chest as you bring your hands together.

items.name: High-to-Low Cable Fly
items.summary: The classic cable crossover: the cables pull from above and you sweep your hands down and together, emphasising the lower chest.

items.name: Low-to-High Cable Fly
items.summary: A cable fly from low pulleys, sweeping the hands up and together to target the upper chest.

items.name: Incline Cable Fly
items.summary: A fly lying on an incline bench between two low cables, which keeps tension on the upper chest even at the top where dumbbells go slack.

items.name: Single-Arm Cable Fly
items.summary: A cable fly done one arm at a time, which lets you bring the hand across the body for a fuller contraction.

items.name: Pec Deck
items.summary: A seated machine fly that brings the arms together in front of the chest along a fixed path. Also called the machine fly.

items.name: Band Chest Fly
items.summary: A standing fly against a resistance band anchored behind you, a home version of the cable fly.

items.name: Svend Press
items.summary: A standing press with one or two weight plates squeezed together between your palms, pushed straight out from the chest to keep the inner chest working hard.

items.name: Push-Up
items.summary: The fundamental bodyweight press: lower your chest to the floor from a plank and push back up.

items.name: Wall Push-Up
items.summary: A push-up against a wall, the easiest version and a good starting point for building up to floor push-ups.

items.name: Incline Push-Up
items.summary: A push-up with your hands raised on a bench or box, which lightens the load and is a common step toward full push-ups.

items.name: Knee Push-Up
items.summary: A push-up done from the knees, which shortens the lever so beginners can work the full range.

items.name: Wide Push-Up
items.summary: A push-up with the hands set wide, which puts more of the work on the chest and less on the triceps.

items.name: Decline Push-Up
items.summary: A push-up with your feet raised on a bench or box, which adds load and shifts the work toward the upper chest and front delts.

items.name: Deficit Push-Up
items.summary: A push-up with the hands on blocks, plates or handles so the chest can sink below hand level for a deeper stretch.

items.name: Banded Push-Up
items.summary: A push-up with a resistance band across your upper back, adding resistance that grows as you push to the top.

items.name: Weighted Push-Up
items.summary: A push-up with a weight plate on your upper back or a weighted vest, for when bodyweight reps get too easy.

items.name: Archer Push-Up
items.summary: A very wide push-up where you shift your weight over one arm while the other stays nearly straight, a step toward the one-arm push-up.

items.name: Ring Push-Up
items.summary: A push-up on gymnastic rings or a suspension trainer; the unstable handles make the chest and shoulders work harder to stay steady.

items.name: One-Arm Push-Up
items.summary: A push-up on a single arm with the feet set wide, demanding serious pressing strength and full-body tension.

items.name: Chest Dip
items.summary: A dip on parallel bars with the torso leaning forward, which loads the lower chest along with the triceps and front delts.

items.name: Assisted Chest Dip
items.summary: A chest dip on an assisted dip machine, where a counterweight takes off part of your bodyweight so you can learn the movement.

items.name: Weighted Chest Dip
items.summary: A chest dip with extra weight hung from a dip belt or held between the feet, for lifters who can already do plenty of bodyweight dips.

items.name: Ring Dip
items.summary: A dip on gymnastic rings, much harder than bar dips because you have to stop the rings swinging out while you press.

items.name: Dumbbell Pullover
items.summary: A lying movement that swings a dumbbell from over your chest to behind your head and back, working the chest and lats together through a big stretch.

items.name: Push-Up Plus
items.summary: A push-up with an extra push at the top to spread the shoulder blades apart, training the serratus anterior that holds the shoulder blade to the ribs.

items.name: Scapular Push-Up
items.summary: A small plank movement where only the shoulder blades move, squeezing together and then spreading apart, to train the serratus anterior and shoulder blade control.

items.name: Dumbbell Serratus Punch
items.summary: A lying punch toward the ceiling with a dumbbell that trains the serratus anterior, a common physio exercise for shoulder blade control.

items.name: Wall Slide with Lift-Off
items.summary: A wall slide with the forearms on the wall followed by lifting the hands off at the top, training the serratus anterior and lower traps that rotate the shoulder blade upward.

items.name: Crunch
items.summary: The basic ab exercise: lying on your back, you curl your shoulders off the floor by shortening your abs.

items.name: Weighted Crunch
items.summary: A crunch with a dumbbell or plate held on your chest, so you can train the abs with progressive load.

items.name: Decline Crunch
items.summary: A crunch on a decline bench with your feet hooked, which lengthens the range and makes the abs work harder.

items.name: Reverse Crunch
items.summary: Curls the pelvis up toward the ribs instead of the shoulders toward the hips, with a focus on the lower abs.

items.name: Toe Touch Crunch
items.summary: A crunch with your legs pointed straight up, reaching your hands toward your toes.

items.name: Stability Ball Crunch
items.summary: A crunch on a stability ball, which lets your spine extend over the ball for a longer range of motion.

items.name: Cable Crunch
items.summary: A kneeling crunch against a high cable, one of the best ways to load the abs heavily.

items.name: Machine Crunch
items.summary: A seated ab crunch machine that guides the movement and makes it easy to add load.

items.name: Sit-Up
items.summary: A full sit-up from lying to upright, working the abs together with the hip flexors.

items.name: Decline Sit-Up
items.summary: A full sit-up on a decline bench with feet anchored, harder than a flat sit-up as the angle increases.

items.name: Weighted Sit-Up
items.summary: A sit-up holding a weight plate on your chest, a simple way to add load once bodyweight sit-ups are easy.

items.name: V-Up
items.summary: Lifting your straight legs and torso at the same time to meet in a V, a hard full-range ab exercise.

items.name: Tuck-Up
items.summary: An easier V-up where you bring bent knees and torso together into a tuck.

items.name: Lying Leg Raise
items.summary: Lying on your back and raising straight legs to vertical, training the lower abs and hip flexors.

items.name: Flutter Kicks
items.summary: Small, quick alternating kicks with straight legs held just off the floor, an endurance drill for the lower abs and hip flexors.

items.name: Hanging Knee Raise
items.summary: Hanging from a bar and drawing your knees up toward your chest, the entry point to hanging ab work.

items.name: Hanging Leg Raise
items.summary: Hanging from a bar and raising straight legs up in front of you, a demanding lower-ab and hip-flexor exercise.

items.name: Captain's Chair Knee Raise
items.summary: Knee raises on a captain's chair station, supported on your forearms with your back against the pad.

items.name: Toes-to-Bar
items.summary: Hanging from a bar and raising your feet all the way up to touch it, combining a full leg raise with a lat pull.

items.name: Dragon Flag
items.summary: Lying on a bench holding it behind your head and lowering your rigid body from vertical, one of the hardest core exercises.

items.name: Front Plank
items.summary: Holding a straight body on your forearms and toes, the standard exercise for core endurance and resisting arching.

items.name: High Plank
items.summary: A plank held on straight arms in the top of a push-up position.

items.name: RKC Plank
items.summary: A short, maximal-tension plank where you squeeze everything and pull your elbows toward your feet.

items.name: Long-Lever Plank
items.summary: A forearm plank with your elbows placed well forward of your shoulders, which greatly increases the load on the abs.

items.name: Side Plank
items.summary: Holding your body straight on one forearm and the side of your foot, training the obliques and the deep side core.

items.name: Side Plank Hip Dip
items.summary: A side plank where you lower your hip toward the floor and lift it back up, adding movement to the oblique work.

items.name: Plank Shoulder Tap
items.summary: In a high plank, tapping each hand to the opposite shoulder while keeping your hips still, an anti-rotation drill.

items.name: Body Saw
items.summary: A forearm plank with your feet on sliders or in suspension straps, rocking your body forward and back to load the abs.

items.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
items.summary: From your knees, rolling an ab wheel forward and pulling it back, a strong anti-extension exercise for the abs.

items.name: Standing Ab Wheel Rollout
items.summary: An ab wheel rollout from standing, rolling all the way out until your body is near the floor and back.

items.name: Barbell Rollout
items.summary: A kneeling rollout using a loaded barbell with round plates instead of an ab wheel.

items.name: Stability Ball Rollout
items.summary: A kneeling rollout with your forearms on a stability ball, an easier way to learn anti-extension.

items.name: Stir the Pot
items.summary: A forearm plank on a stability ball, drawing small circles with your elbows to challenge the core in every direction.

items.name: Pallof Press
items.summary: Standing side-on to a cable and pressing the handle straight out, resisting the pull to rotate.

items.name: Band Pallof Press
items.summary: A Pallof press using a resistance band anchored at chest height, easy to do at home.

items.name: High-to-Low Cable Woodchop
items.summary: Pulling a cable diagonally from above one shoulder down across your body to the opposite hip, training rotation through the obliques.

items.name: Low-to-High Cable Woodchop
items.summary: Pulling a cable diagonally from beside one knee up across your body above the opposite shoulder.

items.name: Landmine Rotation
items.summary: Swinging the end of a landmine barbell in an arc from one hip to the other, training rotational strength.

items.name: Russian Twist
items.summary: Sitting leaned back and rotating your torso side to side, an oblique exercise often done holding a weight.

items.name: Lying Windshield Wiper
items.summary: Lying on your back with legs raised and lowering them side to side, a rotational exercise for the obliques.

items.name: Hanging Windshield Wiper
items.summary: Hanging from a bar with your legs raised toward it and rotating them from side to side, an advanced oblique exercise.

items.name: Suitcase Hold
items.summary: Standing tall holding a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell in one hand, resisting the pull to lean sideways.

items.name: Dead Bug
items.summary: Lying on your back and slowly extending opposite arm and leg while keeping your lower back still, teaching core control.

items.name: Bird Dog
items.summary: On hands and knees, reaching opposite arm and leg out long while keeping your spine still, for back and core stability.

items.name: Hollow Body Hold
items.summary: Holding a curved, banana-shaped position on your back with arms and legs off the floor, a gymnastics core staple.

items.name: Hollow Rock
items.summary: Rocking back and forth while holding the hollow body position.

items.name: Tuck L-Sit
items.summary: Supporting yourself on straight arms with your knees tucked to your chest and feet off the floor, the step before a full L-sit.

items.name: L-Sit
items.summary: Supporting yourself on straight arms with legs held straight out in front, demanding strength in the abs, hip flexors and shoulders.

items.name: Dumbbell Side Bend
items.summary: Standing with a dumbbell in one hand and bending sideways down and up, training the obliques and QL.

items.name: Cable Side Bend
items.summary: A side bend holding a low cable handle, giving constant tension on the obliques.

items.name: 45° Side Bend
items.summary: Lying sideways on a 45° back extension bench and raising your torso, a hard oblique and QL exercise.

items.name: Oblique Crunch
items.summary: A crunch with your knees dropped to one side, so the curl comes more from the obliques.

items.name: Bicycle Crunch
items.summary: A crunch where you bring each elbow toward the opposite knee in a pedalling motion, working abs and obliques.

items.name: Heel Taps
items.summary: Lying with your shoulders curled up and reaching side to side to tap each heel, a simple oblique exercise.

items.name: Back Squat
items.summary: The king of leg exercises: a barbell squat with the bar on top of your traps (high-bar), building the quads, glutes and the whole trunk.

items.name: Low-Bar Back Squat
items.summary: A back squat with the bar lower on the rear delts, which tilts the torso forward and brings in more hips, letting most lifters move the most weight.

items.name: Front Squat
items.summary: A squat with the bar racked on the front of your shoulders, forcing an upright torso and putting more of the work on the quads and upper back.

items.name: Box Squat
items.summary: A back squat to a box set at parallel or just below, teaching depth and a strong hip drive from a dead stop.

items.name: Pause Squat
items.summary: A back squat with a 2–3 second pause at the bottom, removing the bounce to build strength and control out of the hole.

items.name: Safety Bar Squat
items.summary: A back squat with a safety squat bar, whose padded yoke and forward handles spare the shoulders and load the upper back and quads hard.

items.name: Zercher Squat
items.summary: A squat with the barbell held in the crooks of your elbows, which hammers the quads, core and upper back.

items.name: Smith Machine Squat
items.summary: A back squat on the Smith machine; the fixed bar path lets you place your feet forward and focus on pushing with the quads.

items.name: Hack Squat
items.summary: A machine squat with your back on an angled pad, letting you squat deep and load the quads without balancing a bar.

items.name: Belt Squat
items.summary: A squat with the load hung from a hip belt, training the legs hard with no weight on the spine.

items.name: Pendulum Squat
items.summary: A machine squat on a swinging arm that keeps resistance high at the bottom, giving the quads a deep, heavy stretch.

items.name: Goblet Squat
items.summary: A squat holding a dumbbell at your chest; the front load keeps you upright, making it the best way to learn to squat.

items.name: Kettlebell Goblet Squat
items.summary: A goblet squat holding a kettlebell by the horns at your chest, training the quads and glutes with an upright torso.

items.name: Sumo Goblet Squat
items.summary: A wide-stance squat holding a dumbbell between your legs, working the quads, adductors and glutes.

items.name: Heels-Elevated Goblet Squat
items.summary: A goblet squat with your heels raised on a plate or wedge, letting your knees travel forward to bias the quads and squat deeper.

items.name: Dumbbell Squat
items.summary: A squat holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, a simple way to load the legs without a barbell.

items.name: Bodyweight Squat
items.summary: The basic air squat: sitting down and standing up with no load, for warm-ups, beginners and high-rep work.

items.name: Cossack Squat
items.summary: A deep side-to-side squat onto one leg while the other stays straight, building quads, adductors and hip mobility.

items.name: Split Squat
items.summary: A static lunge with both feet planted, one forward and one back, lowering straight down to train one leg at a time.

items.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
items.summary: A split squat with your rear foot up on a bench, one of the hardest and most effective single-leg exercises for the quads and glutes.

items.name: Pistol Squat
items.summary: A full single-leg squat with the other leg held straight out in front, demanding strength, balance and mobility.

items.name: Assisted Pistol Squat
items.summary: A single-leg squat holding a post, doorframe or suspension straps for balance, the stepping stone to a full pistol.

items.name: Shrimp Squat
items.summary: A single-leg squat holding your rear foot behind you and lowering the back knee to the floor, very demanding on the quads.

items.name: Sissy Squat
items.summary: A quad-isolating squat where you lean back and drive your knees forward, keeping your hips extended, for a deep stretch on the front of the thigh.

items.name: Spanish Squat
items.summary: A squat with a heavy band looped behind your knees and anchored in front, letting you sit back with vertical shins to load the quads gently; popular for knee pain.

items.name: Wall Sit
items.summary: An isometric squat held with your back against a wall and thighs parallel to the floor, building quad endurance.

items.name: Dumbbell Lunge
items.summary: A forward lunge holding a dumbbell in each hand, training each leg in turn with a strong deceleration demand.

items.name: Reverse Lunge
items.summary: A lunge stepping backward instead of forward, which is easier on the knees and easier to balance.

items.name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
items.summary: A reverse lunge holding dumbbells at your sides, a knee-friendly way to load each leg.

items.name: Deficit Reverse Lunge
items.summary: A reverse lunge with your front foot on a low step or plate, increasing the range of motion for the quads and glutes.

items.name: Barbell Lunge
items.summary: A lunge with a barbell on your upper back, allowing heavier loading than dumbbells but demanding more balance.

items.name: Walking Lunge
items.summary: Continuous forward lunges, stepping through with each rep to travel across the floor.

items.name: Dumbbell Walking Lunge
items.summary: Walking lunges holding a dumbbell in each hand, a classic leg-day finisher for the quads and glutes.

items.name: Lateral Lunge
items.summary: A side lunge that trains the quads, glutes and adductors in the side-to-side plane.

items.name: Curtsy Lunge
items.summary: A lunge stepping one leg diagonally behind the other, adding glute medius and adductor work to the quads.

items.name: Dumbbell Step-Up
items.summary: Stepping up onto a box or bench holding dumbbells, training each leg's quads and glutes.

items.name: Box Step-Up
items.summary: A bodyweight step-up onto a box or step, a simple single-leg exercise for strength and knee control.

items.name: Barbell Step-Up
items.summary: A step-up with a barbell on your back, allowing heavier single-leg loading for the quads and glutes.

items.name: Lateral Step-Up
items.summary: A step-up from the side of a box, training the quads and glute medius together.

items.name: Step-Down
items.summary: Slowly lowering one heel to the floor from a step while balancing on the other leg, building eccentric quad strength and knee control.

items.name: Leg Press
items.summary: Pressing a weighted sled away with your legs, a safe way to load the quads and glutes heavily.

items.name: Single-Leg Leg Press
items.summary: A leg press with one leg at a time, evening out strength differences between sides.

items.name: Narrow-Stance Leg Press
items.summary: A leg press with feet close together low on the platform, shifting the work onto the quads.

items.name: Leg Extension
items.summary: The machine for isolating the quads: straightening your knees against a pad at your ankles.

items.name: Single-Leg Leg Extension
items.summary: A leg extension with one leg at a time, for fixing imbalances and focusing on each quad.

items.name: Reverse Nordic
items.summary: Kneeling and leaning back with a straight body from knees to head, loading the quads in a long stretch.

items.name: Hip Adduction Machine
items.summary: A seated machine that trains the inner-thigh adductors by squeezing your legs together against the pads.

items.name: Cable Hip Adduction
items.summary: A standing adduction with an ankle strap on a low cable, pulling the leg across the body to train the inner thigh.

items.name: Side-Lying Hip Adduction
items.summary: Lying on your side and lifting the bottom leg, a simple floor exercise for the inner thigh.

items.name: Copenhagen Plank
items.summary: A side plank with your top leg on a bench, held by the adductors; proven to reduce groin injuries in field sports.

items.name: Standing Calf Raise
items.summary: Raising your heels with straight knees under a shoulder-pad machine, the main exercise for the gastrocnemius.

items.name: Seated Calf Raise
items.summary: A calf raise sitting with bent knees and a pad on your thighs, which targets the soleus.

items.name: Dumbbell Calf Raise
items.summary: A standing calf raise holding dumbbells, done off a step for a full range.

items.name: Single-Leg Dumbbell Calf Raise
items.summary: A one-leg calf raise off a step holding a dumbbell, a heavy calf exercise that needs no machine.

items.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
items.summary: A bodyweight calf raise on one leg off a step, enough load for most people and a staple of calf and Achilles rehab.

items.name: Bodyweight Calf Raise
items.summary: Rising onto your toes on both feet with no weight, a beginner calf exercise you can do anywhere.

items.name: Leg Press Calf Raise
items.summary: A calf raise done on the leg press, pushing the platform with the balls of your feet.

items.name: Smith Machine Calf Raise
items.summary: A standing calf raise with a Smith machine bar on your back, often done standing on a plate or step.

items.name: Donkey Calf Raise
items.summary: A calf raise bent forward at the hips with the load on your lower back, giving the calves a deep stretch.

items.name: Tibialis Raise
items.summary: Lifting your toes while leaning against a wall to train the tibialis anterior on the front of the shin.

items.name: Seated Tibialis Raise
items.summary: Lifting your toes against a padded load on a tibialis machine or tib bar while seated, a loadable way to train the front of the shin.

items.name: Shoulder CARs
items.summary: Controlled articular rotations for the shoulder: the arm traces the biggest circle it can, slowly, while the rest of the body stays still.

items.name: Hip CARs
items.summary: Controlled articular rotations for the hip: the knee draws a slow, full circle through flexion, abduction, rotation and extension, on all fours or standing.

items.name: Ankle CARs
items.summary: Slow, controlled circles of the ankle through its full range to keep the joint and lower-leg muscles mobile.

items.name: 90/90 Hip Switch
items.summary: Seated hip rotation drill: from the 90/90 position you rotate both legs side to side, taking one hip into internal rotation and the other into external rotation.

items.name: Hip Airplane
items.summary: Single-leg balance drill that rotates the pelvis around the standing hip, training hip rotation control and glute strength.

items.name: Quadruped Rock-Back
items.summary: On hands and knees you rock your hips back toward your heels, working deep hip flexion while keeping a neutral spine.

items.name: Frog Rock-Back
items.summary: Wide-kneed rock-back that opens the adductors (inner thighs) dynamically.

items.name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Rock
items.summary: A dynamic hip flexor opener: from a half-kneeling lunge you rock in and out of the stretch at the front of the rear hip.

items.name: Front-to-Back Leg Swing
items.summary: A warm-up drill that swings a straight leg forward and back, dynamically loosening the hamstrings and hip flexors.

items.name: Side-to-Side Leg Swing
items.summary: A warm-up drill that swings the leg across the body and out to the side, loosening the adductors and outer hip.

items.name: Deep Squat Prying
items.summary: Sit in the bottom of a deep squat and use your elbows and small weight shifts to pry open the hips and ankles. Holding a light kettlebell at the chest makes it easier to stay upright.

items.name: World's Greatest Stretch
items.summary: A flowing lunge sequence that opens the rear hip flexor, the front hip and hamstring, and the upper back in one drill.

items.name: Spiderman Lunge with Rotation
items.summary: From a plank you step one foot outside the hand into a deep lunge, then rotate the chest open, stretching the hip flexors, groin and upper back.

items.name: Walking Lunge with Overhead Reach
items.summary: A warm-up walking lunge with both arms reaching overhead and slightly toward the front leg, stretching the rear hip flexor and the side of the trunk.

items.name: Inchworm
items.summary: Walk your hands out from a forward fold to a plank and back, a warm-up that stretches the hamstrings and wakes up the shoulders and core.

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.summary: On hands and knees you alternate between rounding and arching the spine, moving it gently through flexion and extension.

items.name: Open Book Rotation
items.summary: Side-lying thoracic rotation: the top arm opens like the cover of a book to rotate the upper back and stretch the chest.

items.name: Quadruped Thoracic Rotation
items.summary: On all fours with one hand behind your head, you rotate the upper back down and up, building thoracic rotation without twisting the lower back.

items.name: Thread the Needle
items.summary: On all fours you slide one arm under the other and rest on that shoulder, rotating and stretching the upper back and rear shoulder.

items.name: Prone Scorpion
items.summary: Lying face down, you swing one foot up and across toward the opposite hand, rotating the spine and opening the hip flexors and chest.

items.name: Foam Roller Thoracic Extension
items.summary: Lying over a foam roller, you extend the upper back over it segment by segment to undo a hunched posture.

items.name: Knee-to-Wall Ankle Rock
items.summary: In a half-kneeling or split stance by a wall, you drive the front knee forward over the toes to improve ankle dorsiflexion for squats and lunges.

items.name: Banded Ankle Distraction
items.summary: A heavy band anchored behind you pulls the ankle joint back while you drive the knee forward, freeing up stiff dorsiflexion.

items.name: Band Shoulder Dislocate
items.summary: Holding a light band or dowel with a wide grip, you pass it from in front of your hips over your head to behind your back and back again.

items.name: Arm Circles
items.summary: Straight-arm circles forward and backward, growing from small to large, a simple shoulder warm-up.

items.name: Wrist Circles
items.summary: Slow circles of the wrists in both directions to warm up the wrists and forearms before pressing, handstands or yoga.

items.name: Quadruped Wrist Rocks
items.summary: On all fours you rock your weight over your hands in different positions to prepare the wrists for loaded extension.

items.name: Foam Roll Quads
items.summary: Face-down foam rolling of the front of the thighs to ease stiffness before or after training. Needs a foam roller.

items.name: Foam Roll IT Band
items.summary: Side-lying foam rolling of the outer thigh, from the hip to just above the knee. Needs a foam roller.

items.name: Foam Roll Upper Back
items.summary: Lying back over a foam roller, you roll the muscles between and around the shoulder blades. Needs a foam roller.

items.name: Foam Roll Lats
items.summary: Side-lying foam rolling of the lat, along the side of the back under the armpit. Needs a foam roller.

items.name: Foam Roll Calves
items.summary: Seated foam rolling of the calves, from the ankle to below the knee. Needs a foam roller.

items.name: Foam Roll Glutes
items.summary: Seated foam rolling of the glutes with one ankle crossed over the opposite knee. Needs a foam roller.

items.name: Foam Roll Hamstrings
items.summary: Seated foam rolling of the back of the thighs. Needs a foam roller.

items.name: Lacrosse Ball Pec Release
items.summary: Pinning a lacrosse or massage ball against a wall with your chest to release tight pecs and the front of the shoulder.

items.name: Lacrosse Ball Glute Release
items.summary: Sitting or leaning on a lacrosse or massage ball to work into tight spots in the glutes and deep hip rotators.

items.name: Doorway Chest Stretch
items.summary: With your forearms on a doorframe you step through to stretch the pecs and front delts.

items.name: Behind-the-Back Chest Stretch
items.summary: Clasping your hands behind your back and lifting them away from you to open the chest and front shoulders, no equipment needed.

items.name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
items.summary: Pulling one arm across your chest with the other to stretch the back of the shoulder.

items.name: Sleeper Stretch
items.summary: Lying on your side, you press the forearm toward the floor to stretch the shoulder's internal rotation and the back of the rotator cuff.

items.name: Overhead Triceps Stretch
items.summary: Reaching one hand down your back with the elbow pointing up to stretch the triceps and lats.

items.name: Wall Biceps Stretch
items.summary: With a straight arm against a wall behind you, you turn away to stretch the biceps and front of the shoulder.

items.name: Kneeling Bench Lat Stretch
items.summary: Kneeling in front of a bench with your elbows on it, you sink your chest toward the floor to stretch the lats and triceps.

items.name: Child's Pose Side Reach
items.summary: A child's pose with both hands walked over to one side, stretching the lat and side of the trunk on the opposite side.

items.name: Upper Back Hug Stretch
items.summary: Hugging yourself and rounding forward to spread the shoulder blades and stretch the upper back.

items.name: Wrist Flexor Stretch
items.summary: Pulling the fingers back with the arm straight to stretch the muscles on the palm side of the forearm.

items.name: Wrist Extensor Stretch
items.summary: Bending the hand down with the arm straight to stretch the muscles on the back of the forearm.

items.name: Standing Hamstring Stretch
items.summary: With one heel on a step or low bench, you hinge forward from the hips to stretch the back of the thigh.

items.name: Seated Single-Leg Hamstring Stretch
items.summary: Seated with one leg straight and the other foot tucked in, you fold forward over the straight leg.

items.name: Supine Hamstring Strap Stretch
items.summary: Lying on your back with a strap or band around one foot, you draw the straight leg up to stretch the hamstring without loading the lower back.

items.name: Standing Quad Stretch
items.summary: Standing on one leg, you pull the other heel to your glute to stretch the front of the thigh.

items.name: Side-Lying Quad Stretch
items.summary: Lying on your side, you pull the top heel to your glute: a quad stretch without the balance demand.

items.name: Couch Stretch
items.summary: A deep stretch for the quads and hip flexors with the back knee on the floor and the back shin up against a wall or couch.

items.name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
items.summary: A half-kneeling stretch for the front of the rear hip, made effective by tucking the pelvis and squeezing the glute.

items.name: Sleeping Pigeon Stretch
items.summary: A deep glute and outer hip stretch with the front shin across the mat and the torso folded forward over it.

items.name: Supine Figure-Four Stretch
items.summary: Lying on your back with one ankle crossed over the other knee, you pull the legs in to stretch the glute and piriformis. A knee-friendly alternative to pigeon.

items.name: Supine Glute Stretch
items.summary: Lying on your back, you pull one knee toward the opposite shoulder to stretch the glute.

items.name: Seated Piriformis Stretch
items.summary: Sitting on a chair or bench with one ankle on the opposite knee, you lean forward to stretch the piriformis and deep hip rotators.

items.name: Standing IT Band Stretch
items.summary: Crossing one leg behind the other and leaning away to stretch the outer hip (TFL and glute med) and the top of the IT band.

items.name: Butterfly Stretch
items.summary: Seated with the soles of your feet together and knees out, you lean forward to stretch the inner thighs.

items.name: Frog Stretch
items.summary: A deep static adductor stretch on hands or forearms with the knees wide and shins parallel.

items.name: Kneeling Adductor Stretch
items.summary: On one knee with the other leg straight out to the side, you sit your hips back to stretch the inner thigh of the straight leg.

items.name: Seated Straddle Stretch
items.summary: Seated with the legs spread wide, you fold forward to stretch the adductors and hamstrings.

items.name: Wall Calf Stretch
items.summary: Leaning into a wall with the back leg straight and heel down to stretch the upper calf (gastrocnemius).

items.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Stretch
items.summary: The wall calf stretch with the back knee bent, which shifts the stretch to the lower calf (soleus) and Achilles.

items.name: Heel-Drop Calf Stretch
items.summary: Standing on the edge of a step, you let one heel sink below the step to stretch the calf and Achilles tendon.

items.name: Kneeling Shin Stretch
items.summary: Sitting back on your heels with the tops of your feet flat on the floor to stretch the shins (tibialis anterior) and front of the ankles.

items.name: Knees-to-Chest Stretch
items.summary: Lying on your back, you hug both knees to your chest to gently stretch the lower back and glutes.

items.name: Supine Spinal Twist
items.summary: Lying on your back, you drop both bent knees to one side while the shoulders stay down, stretching the lower back, hips and chest.

items.name: Prone Press-Up
items.summary: A passive back-extension stretch: lying face down, you press your chest up with your arms while the hips and lower back stay relaxed, stretching the abs and hip flexors.

items.name: Standing Side Bend Stretch
items.summary: Standing tall and reaching one arm over your head to the side to stretch the obliques and lats.

items.name: Mountain Pose
items.summary: Mountain Pose (Tadasana), the foundation of every standing pose: standing tall and aligned with every muscle quietly engaged.

items.name: Chair Pose
items.summary: Chair Pose (Utkatasana): a held half-squat with the arms reaching overhead that builds strength in the legs and endurance in the shoulders.

items.name: Warrior I
items.summary: Warrior I (Virabhadrasana I): a deep lunge with the hips squared to the front and arms overhead, strengthening the front leg and stretching the back hip flexor.

items.name: Warrior II
items.summary: Warrior II (Virabhadrasana II): a wide-legged lunge with the hips open to the side and arms reaching front and back.

items.name: Warrior III
items.summary: Warrior III (Virabhadrasana III): balancing on one leg with the torso and back leg in a line parallel to the floor.

items.name: Triangle Pose
items.summary: Triangle Pose (Utthita Trikonasana): with both legs straight, you reach sideways over the front leg to stretch the hamstrings, groin and side of the trunk.

items.name: Extended Side Angle
items.summary: Extended Side Angle (Utthita Parsvakonasana): from Warrior II you lean over the bent front leg and reach the top arm overhead in one long diagonal line.

items.name: Crescent Lunge
items.summary: Crescent Lunge (Ashta Chandrasana): a high lunge with the back heel lifted and arms overhead, building leg strength and balance while stretching the back hip.

items.name: Tree Pose
items.summary: Tree Pose (Vrksasana): a standing balance with the sole of one foot pressed into the inner standing leg.

items.name: Eagle Pose
items.summary: Eagle Pose (Garudasana): a one-legged balance with legs and arms wrapped, strengthening the standing leg and stretching the upper back and outer hips.

items.name: Half Moon Pose
items.summary: Half Moon (Ardha Chandrasana): balancing on one leg and one hand with the body opened sideways and the top leg lifted parallel to the floor.

items.name: Standing Forward Fold
items.summary: Standing Forward Fold (Uttanasana): folding forward from the hips with the head hanging to stretch the hamstrings and lengthen the spine.

items.name: Garland Pose
items.summary: Garland Pose (Malasana): a deep yogi squat with palms together at the chest, opening the hips, groin and ankles.

items.name: Low Lunge
items.summary: Low Lunge (Anjaneyasana): a lunge with the back knee down and arms overhead, a deep stretch for the back hip flexor and thigh.

items.name: Pigeon Pose
items.summary: Pigeon Pose (Eka Pada Rajakapotasana prep): the front shin across the mat and back leg long behind, torso upright, opening the outer hip of the front leg and the hip flexor of the back leg.

items.name: Happy Baby
items.summary: Happy Baby (Ananda Balasana): lying on your back holding your feet with the knees wide, stretching the inner groin and releasing the lower back.

items.name: Child's Pose
items.summary: Child's Pose (Balasana): kneeling and folding forward over the thighs with the arms reaching ahead, a resting pose that gently stretches the back and hips.

items.name: Puppy Pose
items.summary: Puppy Pose (Uttana Shishosana): a cross between Child's Pose and Downward-Facing Dog, with hips high over the knees and chest melting toward the mat to stretch the lats and shoulders.

items.name: Seated Forward Fold
items.summary: Seated Forward Fold (Paschimottanasana): sitting with both legs straight and folding forward over them to stretch the whole back of the body.

items.name: Legs Up the Wall
items.summary: Legs Up the Wall (Viparita Karani): a restorative pose lying on your back with your legs resting up a wall, gently stretching the hamstrings and calming the body.

items.name: Corpse Pose
items.summary: Corpse Pose (Savasana): lying still on your back in complete relaxation, usually at the end of a practice, with slow, easy breathing.

items.name: Cobra Pose
items.summary: Cobra Pose (Bhujangasana): lying face down and lifting the chest with the back muscles, hands lightly supporting, a gentle backbend.

items.name: Upward-Facing Dog
items.summary: Upward-Facing Dog (Urdhva Mukha Svanasana): a backbend on straight arms with the thighs lifted off the floor, opening the chest and front of the body.

items.name: Locust Pose
items.summary: Locust Pose (Salabhasana): lying face down and lifting the chest, arms and legs off the floor to strengthen the whole back of the body.

items.name: Bow Pose
items.summary: Bow Pose (Dhanurasana): lying face down and holding your ankles, you kick into your hands to lift the chest and thighs, a deep backbend.

items.name: Camel Pose
items.summary: Camel Pose (Ustrasana): a kneeling backbend reaching back for the heels, opening the front of the hips, abs and chest.

items.name: Bridge Pose
items.summary: Bridge Pose (Setu Bandha Sarvangasana): lying on your back and lifting the hips high, strengthening the glutes and opening the chest and hip flexors.

items.name: Wheel Pose
items.summary: Wheel Pose (Urdhva Dhanurasana): a full backbend pressing up onto hands and feet, demanding shoulder and spine mobility and strength.

items.name: Downward-Facing Dog
items.summary: Downward-Facing Dog (Adho Mukha Svanasana): an inverted V with hips high, stretching the hamstrings and calves while strengthening the shoulders.

items.name: Plank Pose
items.summary: Plank Pose (Phalakasana): a high plank on straight arms with the body in one line, building core and shoulder strength.

items.name: Side Plank Pose
items.summary: Side Plank (Vasisthasana): balancing on one straight arm and the side of the feet, strengthening the obliques, shoulders and outer hips.

items.name: Chaturanga
items.summary: Chaturanga (Chaturanga Dandasana), four-limbed staff pose: lowering from plank to hover just above the floor with the elbows hugging the ribs.

items.name: Boat Pose
items.summary: Boat Pose (Navasana): balancing on your sit bones with the legs and chest lifted into a V, a strong core hold.

items.name: Crow Pose
items.summary: Crow Pose (Bakasana): balancing on your hands with the knees resting on the backs of the upper arms, the classic first arm balance.

items.name: Sun Salutation A
items.summary: Sun Salutation A (Surya Namaskar A): the classic flowing sequence linking Mountain, Forward Fold, Plank, Chaturanga, Upward Dog and Downward Dog with the breath.

items.name: Plate Neck Flexion
items.summary: Strengthens the front of the neck: lying face up on a bench with your head off the end, you curl your chin toward your chest against a light plate held on your forehead.

items.name: Plate Neck Extension
items.summary: Strengthens the back of the neck: lying face down on a bench with your head off the end, you raise your head against a light plate held on the back of your head.

items.name: Plate Lateral Neck Flexion
items.summary: Strengthens the sides of the neck: lying on your side on a bench with your head off the end, you lift your ear toward your shoulder against a light plate.

items.name: Neck Harness Extension
items.summary: The classic loaded neck extension: wearing a head harness with a weight hanging from it, you lean forward, seated or standing, and raise your head against the load.

items.name: Harness Band Neck Extension
items.summary: A neck harness clipped to a resistance band instead of a weight, giving smooth, joint-friendly tension for neck extension that's easy to set up at home or ringside.

items.name: Cable Neck Extension
items.summary: Neck extension with a head harness clipped to a low cable, which keeps constant tension through the whole range.

items.name: Cable Neck Flexion
items.summary: Neck flexion with a head harness clipped to a cable behind you; you nod your chin toward your chest against the pull.

items.name: Cable Lateral Neck Flexion
items.summary: Side bending of the neck against a cable attached to a head harness, standing side-on to the stack.

items.name: Band Neck Flexion
items.summary: Strengthens the front of the neck with a light band anchored behind you and looped around your forehead.

items.name: Band Neck Extension
items.summary: Strengthens the back of the neck with a light band anchored in front of you and looped around the back of your head.

items.name: Band Lateral Neck Flexion
items.summary: Strengthens the sides of the neck with a light band anchored beside you and looped around the side of your head.

items.name: Band Neck Rotation
items.summary: Trains the neck rotators by turning your head against a light band, useful for athletes who need to resist twisting forces.

items.name: Band Chin Tuck
items.summary: A chin tuck against a band around the back of your head, training the deep neck muscles that hold your head back over your shoulders.

items.name: 4-Way Neck Machine
items.summary: A pad-and-stack machine that loads the neck in all four directions: forward, back and both sides.

items.name: Machine Neck Flexion
items.summary: Forward neck flexion on a 4-way neck machine, with the pad on your forehead.

items.name: Machine Neck Extension
items.summary: Neck extension on a 4-way neck machine, with the pad on the back of your head.

items.name: Machine Lateral Neck Flexion
items.summary: Side bending on a 4-way neck machine, with the pad on the side of your head.

items.name: Isometric Neck Hold (Front and Back)
items.summary: Hand-resisted isometric holds for the front and back of the neck: you press your head into your hands while they stop it moving.

items.name: Isometric Neck Hold (Sides)
items.summary: Hand-resisted isometric holds for the sides of the neck: you press your head sideways into your hand while it stops it moving.

items.name: Isometric Neck Hold (Rotation)
items.summary: Hand-resisted isometric hold for the neck rotators: you try to turn your head into your hand while it stops it moving.

items.name: Partner Neck Isometrics
items.summary: A partner pushes on your head from the front, back and sides while you hold your head still, the way wrestlers and fighters build neck strength.

items.name: Partner Manual Neck Resistance
items.summary: A partner applies hand resistance as you move your head through each direction, a staple of wrestling and rugby neck training that needs no equipment.

items.name: Swiss Ball Neck Hold (Front)
items.summary: An isometric hold for the front of the neck: you lean your forehead into a Swiss ball pinned against a wall.

items.name: Swiss Ball Neck Hold (Back)
items.summary: An isometric hold for the back of the neck: you lean the back of your head into a Swiss ball pinned against a wall.

items.name: Swiss Ball Neck Hold (Side)
items.summary: An isometric hold for the side of the neck: you lean the side of your head into a Swiss ball pinned against a wall.

items.name: Lying Neck Curl
items.summary: A bodyweight neck flexion lying face up with your head off the end of a bench, the first step before adding a plate.

items.name: Lying Neck Extension
items.summary: A bodyweight neck extension lying face down with your head off the end of a bench.

items.name: Side-Lying Neck Raise
items.summary: A bodyweight side bend of the neck lying on your side, with your head off the end of a bench or lifted off the floor.

items.name: Wall Neck Bridge
items.summary: A leaning bridge with your head on a padded wall, the safe progression toward floor neck bridges; done facing the wall and with your back to it.

items.name: Wrestler's Bridge
items.summary: The wrestler's back bridge: lying face up, you arch and lift your hips so your weight rests on your feet and the top of your head, building a strong, resilient back of the neck.

items.name: Front Neck Bridge
items.summary: The face-down bridge: with your forehead on the mat and your hips raised, you hold your weight on your head and feet, building strength in the front of the neck.

items.name: Neck Bridge Rocks
items.summary: Slow rocks forward and back in a wrestler's bridge, rolling from the top of your head toward your forehead to strengthen the neck through its range.

items.name: Chin Tuck
items.summary: A small backward glide of the head that trains the deep neck flexors and counters forward-head posture.

items.name: Wall Chin Tuck
items.summary: A chin tuck standing with your back against a wall, using the wall as a guide and as light resistance.

items.name: Lying Chin Nod
items.summary: A gentle nodding movement lying face up with your head on the floor (craniocervical flexion), the physio's first exercise for the deep neck flexors.

items.name: Supine Chin Tuck Head Lift
items.summary: Lying face up, you tuck your chin and lift your head just off the floor, training the deep neck flexors for strength and endurance.

items.name: Prone Chin Tuck Head Lift
items.summary: Lying face down, you tuck your chin and lift your forehead just off the floor, training the deep neck extensors.

items.name: Quadruped Neck Extension
items.summary: On hands and knees, you lower and raise your head with your chin tucked, a controlled way to train the neck extensors through range.

items.name: Neck CARs
items.summary: Controlled articular rotations for the neck: slow, deliberate circles through the largest pain-free range to keep the joints moving well.

items.name: Controlled Neck Rotation
items.summary: Slowly turning the head from side to side to maintain rotation range.

items.name: Neck Side Tilt
items.summary: Slowly tilting your ear toward each shoulder to keep side-bending range in the neck.

items.name: Upper Trap Stretch
items.summary: A lateral neck stretch for the side of the neck and upper traps: you tilt your ear toward one shoulder and gently assist with your hand.

items.name: Levator Scapulae Stretch
items.summary: Stretches the levator scapulae, the muscle from the neck to the top of the shoulder blade, by turning your nose toward your armpit and looking down.

items.name: SCM Stretch
items.summary: Stretches the sternocleidomastoid at the front and side of the neck by tilting your head away and looking slightly up.

items.name: Scalene Stretch
items.summary: Stretches the scalenes on the side of the neck by anchoring your collarbone and tilting your head away and slightly back.

items.name: Neck Extensor Stretch
items.summary: Stretches the back of the neck by lowering your chin toward your chest with gentle help from your hands.

items.name: Suboccipital Release
items.summary: Eases tension in the small muscles at the base of the skull with a gentle chin nod, lying with your head supported on your fingertips or two tennis balls.

items.name: The Hundred
items.summary: The classical warm-up: a held abdominal curl with legs extended while the arms pump in time with the breath for 100 counts.

items.name: Roll-Up
items.summary: A slow articulation of the spine from lying to a forward reach over the legs and back down, one vertebra at a time.

items.name: Roll-Over
items.summary: Lift the legs overhead and roll the spine up off the mat, then roll it down with control while the legs stay long.

items.name: Single-Leg Circles
items.summary: Trace circles with one straight leg toward the ceiling while the pelvis stays perfectly still, training hip control and core stability.

items.name: Rolling Like a Ball
items.summary: Balance in a tight ball and roll back to the shoulder blades and up again, massaging the spine and teaching abdominal control.

items.name: Single-Leg Stretch
items.summary: The first of the abdominal series: hold a chest curl while drawing one knee in and extending the other leg, switching rhythmically.

items.name: Double-Leg Stretch
items.summary: From a tight ball in a chest curl, reach the arms and legs away in opposite directions, then circle the arms back and hug in.

items.name: Single Straight-Leg Stretch
items.summary: Often called scissors on the mat: hold a chest curl and scissor straight legs, pulsing one toward you as the other hovers.

items.name: Double Straight-Leg Stretch
