items.summary: Also known as the lower lift: hands behind the head in a chest curl, lower both straight legs together and lift them back up.

items.name: Criss-Cross
items.summary: The last of the abdominal series: rotate the curled torso toward the bent knee as the other leg extends, working the obliques.

items.name: Spine Stretch Forward
items.summary: Sit tall with legs apart and round forward over a deep abdominal scoop, articulating the spine down and back up to vertical.

items.name: Open-Leg Rocker
items.summary: Balance with straight legs in a V holding your ankles, then rock back to the shoulder blades and up again without losing the shape.

items.name: Corkscrew
items.summary: With legs glued together toward the ceiling, circle them side to side around the centre line, challenging the obliques and pelvic stability.

items.name: Saw
items.summary: Sitting with legs apart, twist and reach the little finger past the opposite little toe, sawing it off, to train rotation and flexion together.

items.name: Swan Dive
items.summary: Press into a full back extension, then release the hands and rock forward and back on the front of the body in a strong arched shape.

items.name: Single-Leg Kick
items.summary: Lift onto the forearms in a sphinx position and kick each heel toward the seat with a double beat, working the hamstrings while the trunk stays lifted.

items.name: Double-Leg Kick
items.summary: Lying face down with hands clasped high on the back, kick both heels toward the seat, then extend the legs and lift the chest as the arms reach back.

items.name: Neck Pull
items.summary: A harder Roll-Up with hands behind the head: curl up, round forward, sit tall, then hinge back and roll down slowly.

items.name: Pilates Scissors
items.summary: Lifted into a supported shoulder stand, split the legs forward and back in a scissor, training control and hip mobility while inverted.

items.name: Pilates Bicycle
items.summary: From the supported shoulder stand of Scissors, pedal the legs in a large backward bicycle, adding knee bend to the split.

items.name: Shoulder Bridge
items.summary: Hold a high bridge on one leg while the other kicks up to the ceiling and lowers with a flexed foot, testing pelvic stability.

items.name: Spine Twist
items.summary: Sit tall with arms out to the sides and twist the spine with a double pulse each way, growing taller as you rotate.

items.name: Pilates Jackknife
items.summary: Roll the legs overhead, then shoot them straight up to the ceiling with the hips lifted and roll down with control.

items.name: Side Kick Front and Back
items.summary: Lying on your side, kick the top leg forward with a double pulse and sweep it back, keeping the torso still to work the hips and core.

items.name: Side Kick Up and Down
items.summary: In the side kick position, kick the top leg up to the ceiling and lower it slowly with resistance, working the outer hip.

items.name: Side Kick Small Circles
items.summary: Hold the top leg at hip height and draw small, precise circles, building endurance in the outer hip.

items.name: Teaser
items.summary: Roll up into a V-sit balance with legs and arms reaching on the diagonal, then roll down with control: Pilates' signature test of core strength.

items.name: Pilates Hip Circles
items.summary: Lean back on straight arms and circle straight legs together in a large arc, challenging the abdominals and shoulder stability.

items.name: Pilates Swimming
items.summary: Lying face down with arms and legs lifted, flutter opposite arm and leg quickly as if swimming, strengthening the back extensors.

items.name: Leg Pull Front
items.summary: Hold a full plank and lift one leg up and down at a time, rocking the heels, to train the core, shoulders and hip extensors.

items.name: Leg Pull Back
items.summary: Hold a reverse plank facing up and kick one straight leg to the ceiling at a time, working the back of the body and the shoulders.

items.name: Kneeling Side Kick
items.summary: From kneeling with one hand on the mat and the other behind the head, kick the top leg forward and back at hip height.

items.name: Pilates Side Bend
items.summary: From a side sit, lift into a full side plank with the top arm arching overhead, then lower with control, working the obliques.

items.name: Boomerang
items.summary: A flowing advanced sequence: roll over with crossed legs, switch them, roll up into teaser, sweep the arms behind and fold forward.

items.name: Seal
items.summary: A playful rolling exercise: hold your ankles from the inside, clap the feet three times, roll back and up again in balance.

items.name: Control Balance
items.summary: From a Roll-Over position, hold one foot overhead and lift the other leg to the ceiling, switching legs with control.

items.name: Pilates Push-Up
items.summary: The closing exercise of the mat: roll down from standing, walk out to plank, do push-ups with the elbows hugging in, then walk back and roll up.

items.name: Pelvic Curl
items.summary: Peel the spine up off the mat into a bridge one vertebra at a time and lay it back down, teaching spinal articulation and glute control.

items.name: Chest Lift
items.summary: The foundational Pilates abdominal curl: lift the head and shoulders on the exhale with a scooped belly and lower on the inhale.

items.name: Pilates Toe Taps
items.summary: From tabletop, lower one foot at a time to tap the mat while the pelvis stays still, training deep abdominal control.

items.name: Pilates Clam
items.summary: Lying on your side with knees bent, open the top knee like a clamshell while the feet stay together, targeting the glute medius.

items.name: Side-Lying Double Leg Lift
items.summary: Lying on your side, lift both legs together off the mat and lower them, working the obliques and side of the trunk.

items.name: Side-Lying Inner Thigh Lift
items.summary: With the top leg crossed in front, lift and lower the straight bottom leg to work the inner thigh (adductors).

items.name: Swan Prep
items.summary: A gentle back extension from lying face down, lifting the head and chest with the hands lightly on the mat.

items.name: Mermaid
items.summary: A seated side bend in a Z-sit with the arm reaching overhead, stretching and strengthening the sides of the body.

items.name: Reformer Footwork
items.summary: The reformer warm-up: lying on the carriage with feet on the footbar, press out and return in a series of foot positions (toes, arches, heels, V).

items.name: Reformer Hundred
items.summary: The Hundred lying on the carriage holding the straps, so the arms pump against spring resistance.

items.name: Reformer Frog
items.summary: Lying with feet in the straps, heels together and knees open, press the legs out on the diagonal and draw them back in, working the inner thighs and hips.

items.name: Reformer Leg Circles
items.summary: With both feet in the straps, circle the straight legs together against the springs, working the hips and inner thighs with a stable pelvis.

items.name: Reformer Short Spine
items.summary: With feet in the straps, lift the legs over and roll the spine up off the carriage, bend the knees, then roll down bone by bone.

items.name: Reformer Long Stretch
items.summary: Hold a plank with hands on the footbar and feet against the shoulder blocks, pushing the carriage back and pulling it forward from the shoulders.

items.name: Reformer Elephant
items.summary: Standing on the carriage in a pike with hands on the footbar, push the carriage back and forth with the legs while the upper body stays still.

items.name: Reformer Knee Stretches
items.summary: Kneeling on the carriage with hands on the footbar, drive the carriage back and forth with the legs while the trunk holds a fixed shape (round, flat or knees off).

items.name: Reformer Rowing
items.summary: Seated on the carriage holding the straps, a series of arm patterns (from the chest, from the hips, shaving, hug) that combine spinal flexion and extension with upper-body strength.

items.name: Reformer Stomach Massage
items.summary: Seated on the carriage with feet on the footbar, push out and back while holding a rounded, then flat, then twisted trunk position.

items.name: Reformer Side Splits
items.summary: Standing with one foot on the frame and one on the carriage, slide the legs apart and pull them back together, working the inner and outer thighs.

items.name: Reformer Mermaid
items.summary: Sitting sideways on the carriage with one hand on the footbar, push the carriage out into a long side bend, then stretch the other way.

items.name: Reformer Chest Expansion
items.summary: Kneeling on the carriage facing the straps, pull the arms straight back past the hips, turn the head side to side and return with control.

items.name: Reformer Arms in Straps
items.summary: Lying on the carriage holding the straps, press the arms down to the sides and through other patterns (circles, triceps, adduction) with a stable trunk.

items.name: Reformer Running
items.summary: Part of the footwork series: with the legs straight and the carriage out, alternately lower one heel under the footbar as the other knee bends, like running in place.

items.name: Reformer Bridging
items.summary: With feet on the footbar, roll up into a bridge and then press the carriage out and in from the bridge, working the glutes and hamstrings.

items.name: Reformer Pulling Straps
items.summary: Lying face down on the long box holding the straps, pull the straight arms back alongside the body as the chest lifts into extension.

items.name: Reformer Backstroke
items.summary: Seated on the long box in a ball holding the straps, reach the arms and legs to the ceiling, open them wide and circle back to the ball.

items.name: Reformer Teaser
items.summary: Teaser on the reformer: balancing in a V-sit on the carriage or box, holding the straps, and rolling down and up against the springs.

items.name: Cadillac Roll-Down Bar
items.summary: Sitting facing the roll-down bar, roll back through the spine against the spring and return, an assisted way to learn the Roll-Up.

items.name: Cadillac Leg Springs
items.summary: Lying on the Cadillac with feet in loops attached to springs, work the legs through lowers, frogs, circles and walking against the springs.

items.name: Cadillac Push-Through
items.summary: Sitting facing the tower, push the bar forward and down into a spine stretch, then roll up and lift the bar overhead into extension.

items.name: Chair Footwork
items.summary: Seated tall on the Wunda chair, press the pedal down and up with the feet in several positions, training the legs and an upright spine.

items.name: Chair Pike
items.summary: Standing behind the chair with hands on the pedal, lift the hips high into a pike as the pedal rises, then lower with control.

items.name: Chair Swan
items.summary: Lying face down on the chair seat with hands on the pedal, lift the chest into extension as the pedal rises and lower as you press it down.

items.name: Magic Circle Inner Thigh Squeeze
items.summary: Squeeze a Pilates ring between the thighs or ankles and release with control, working the inner thighs (adductors) and pelvic floor.

items.name: Magic Circle Chest Press
items.summary: Hold a Pilates ring between the palms at chest height and press it, working the chest and the connection between the arms and core.

items.name: Small Ball Roll-Back
items.summary: Sitting with a small soft ball behind the lower back, roll back onto it into a curl and return, building abdominal control with support.

items.name: Deadlift
items.summary: The conventional barbell deadlift: lift the bar from the floor to standing with a flat back, training the whole posterior chain and grip.

items.name: Sumo Deadlift
items.summary: A wide-stance deadlift with the hands inside the knees, giving a more upright torso and more work for the glutes, adductors and quads.

items.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
items.summary: A deadlift with a hexagonal trap bar, standing inside the frame. The load sits in line with your body, so it's easier on the lower back and more quad-heavy.

items.name: Deficit Deadlift
items.summary: A conventional deadlift standing on a 2–10 cm plate or platform, lengthening the range to build strength off the floor.

items.name: Rack Pull
items.summary: A partial deadlift from pins or blocks at about knee height, overloading the lockout and the upper back.

items.name: Stiff-Leg Deadlift
items.summary: A hinge with nearly straight legs where each rep starts from the floor, putting a big stretch on the hamstrings.

items.name: Snatch-Grip Deadlift
items.summary: A deadlift with a very wide grip that makes you start lower, building the upper back, grip and strength off the floor.

items.name: Paused Deadlift
items.summary: A deadlift with a 1–3 second pause just after the bar leaves the floor or at the knee, teaching position and control.

items.name: Kettlebell Deadlift
items.summary: A deadlift with a kettlebell between your feet, the easiest way to learn the hip hinge.

items.name: Romanian Deadlift
items.summary: A top-down barbell hinge with soft knees, lowering the bar along your legs until the hamstrings are fully stretched.

items.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
items.summary: The Romanian deadlift with a dumbbell in each hand, hinging until the hamstrings are fully stretched.

items.name: Single-Leg RDL
items.summary: A bodyweight Romanian deadlift on one leg that trains the hamstrings, glutes and balance.

items.name: Single-Leg Dumbbell RDL
items.summary: A single-leg Romanian deadlift holding a dumbbell, loading each hamstring and glute on its own.

items.name: B-Stance Dumbbell RDL
items.summary: A Romanian deadlift with most of your weight on the front leg and the back foot as a kickstand, a stable step toward single-leg work.

items.name: Landmine RDL
items.summary: A Romanian deadlift holding the end of a landmine-anchored barbell, whose arc makes the hinge easy to learn.

items.name: Lying Leg Curl
items.summary: A machine curl lying face down, bending your knees to bring the pad toward your glutes.

items.name: Seated Leg Curl
items.summary: A machine curl sitting upright, which trains the hamstrings in a lengthened position.

items.name: Standing Leg Curl
items.summary: A one-leg-at-a-time machine curl done standing, letting you focus on each hamstring.

items.name: Cable Standing Leg Curl
items.summary: A standing single-leg curl with an ankle strap on a low cable, for when there's no leg curl machine.

items.name: Dumbbell Lying Leg Curl
items.summary: A leg curl lying face down on a bench with a dumbbell held between your feet.

items.name: Swiss Ball Leg Curl
items.summary: A hamstring curl lying on your back with your heels on a stability ball, rolling it in while holding your hips up.

items.name: Slider Leg Curl
items.summary: A bridge-position hamstring curl sliding your heels on gliders or a towel on a smooth floor.

items.name: Nordic Curl
items.summary: An eccentric hamstring exercise: kneel with your ankles anchored and lower your body toward the floor as slowly as you can.

items.name: Glute-Ham Raise
items.summary: Done on a glute-ham developer (GHD): extend your hips and then curl your body up with your hamstrings.

items.name: Razor Curl
items.summary: A Nordic curl variant where you hinge at the hips as you lower and then curl your body back up, making it easier to come back up.

items.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
items.summary: With your upper back on a bench, drive a barbell up with your hips. One of the best loaded glute exercises.

items.name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
items.summary: A hip thrust with a dumbbell resting across your hips, ideal for lighter loads or home training.

items.name: Smith Machine Hip Thrust
items.summary: A hip thrust under a Smith machine bar, which keeps the bar path fixed and is easy to set up.

items.name: Machine Hip Thrust
items.summary: A hip thrust on a dedicated hip thrust or glute drive machine, with a belt or pad over your hips.

items.name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust
items.summary: A bodyweight hip thrust on one leg with your upper back on a bench, training each glute alone.

items.name: B-Stance Hip Thrust
items.summary: A barbell hip thrust with one foot forward as a kickstand, putting most of the load on one glute.

items.name: Glute Bridge
items.summary: Lying on your back with knees bent, lift your hips by squeezing your glutes. The basic glute exercise.

items.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
items.summary: A glute bridge on one leg, with the other leg extended or held up.

items.name: Barbell Glute Bridge
items.summary: A glute bridge from the floor with a barbell over your hips, a shorter-range alternative to the hip thrust.

items.name: Banded Glute Bridge
items.summary: A glute bridge with a mini band just above your knees, adding glute medius work as you push your knees out.

items.name: Frog Pump
items.summary: A short glute bridge with the soles of your feet together and knees open, usually done for high reps.

items.name: Cable Glute Kickback
items.summary: A standing kickback with an ankle strap on a low cable, extending the hip against resistance.

items.name: Machine Glute Kickback
items.summary: A kickback on a glute kickback machine, pressing a pad or platform back with one leg.

items.name: Band Glute Kickback
items.summary: A kickback against a resistance band, done on all fours or standing, for home training.

items.name: Donkey Kick
items.summary: On all fours, drive one bent leg up toward the ceiling, sole first, to work the glute.

items.name: Quadruped Hip Extension
items.summary: On all fours, extend one straight leg back to hip height, training the glute and hamstring.

items.name: Hip Abduction Machine
items.summary: A seated machine where you push your legs apart against the pads, training the glute medius and outer hip.

items.name: Cable Hip Abduction
items.summary: A standing side leg raise with an ankle strap on a low cable, training the glute medius.

items.name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
items.summary: Lying on your side, lift your straight top leg toward the ceiling to train the glute medius.

items.name: Clamshell
items.summary: Lying on your side with knees bent, open your top knee like a clam shell to train the glute medius.

items.name: Banded Lateral Walk
items.summary: Sidesteps in a half-squat with a mini band around your legs, a common glute medius warm-up.

items.name: Monster Walk
items.summary: Walking forward and backward in wide diagonal steps with a mini band around your legs, working the glute medius.

items.name: Fire Hydrant
items.summary: On all fours, lift one bent leg out to the side, training the glute medius and hip rotators.

items.name: Side Plank Hip Abduction
items.summary: Holding a side plank, lift your top leg, training the glute medius of both legs and the obliques.

items.name: Banded Seated Hip Abduction
items.summary: Seated on a bench with a mini band above your knees, push your knees out. A band version of the abduction machine.

items.name: Back Extension
items.summary: On a horizontal (90°) back extension bench or roman chair, lower your torso and raise it back in line with your legs.

items.name: 45° Back Extension
items.summary: A back extension on the angled 45° bench, the hyperextension bench most gyms have.

items.name: Back Extension Machine
items.summary: A seated selectorised machine where you extend your back against a pad behind your shoulders.

items.name: Reverse Hyperextension
items.summary: Lying face down on a reverse hyper machine with your legs hanging, swing your legs up behind you, training the lower back and glutes.

items.name: Superman
items.summary: Lying face down, lift your arms, chest and legs off the floor together, training the back extensors.

items.name: Good Morning
items.summary: With a barbell on your upper back, hinge forward at the hips with soft knees and stand back up.

items.name: Banded Good Morning
items.summary: A good morning with a resistance band under your feet and around your neck or upper back, for learning the hinge at home.

items.name: Cable Pull-Through
items.summary: Facing away from a low cable with a rope between your legs, hinge and drive your hips forward to pull it through.

items.name: Jefferson Curl
items.summary: A slow, light-weight curl down through the spine one segment at a time, for spinal flexion strength and hamstring flexibility. Only for people without back problems.

items.name: Box Jump
items.summary: An explosive jump onto a box that trains leg power while keeping landing impact low.

items.name: Seated Box Jump
items.summary: A box jump started from sitting on a bench, removing the countermovement to build starting power.

items.name: Depth Jump
items.summary: A shock-method plyometric: step off a box, land, and rebound into a maximal jump as fast as possible.

items.name: Countermovement Jump
items.summary: The standard vertical jump: a quick dip and arm swing straight into a maximal jump.

items.name: Broad Jump
items.summary: A standing long jump for horizontal power through the hips.

items.name: Tuck Jump
items.summary: A vertical jump with the knees pulled to the chest at the top, done in quick repeated reps.

items.name: Split Jump
items.summary: A jumping lunge: explode up from a split stance and switch legs in the air.

items.name: Single-Leg Hop
items.summary: Hops forward or in place on one leg to build single-leg power, stiffness and landing control.

items.name: Lateral Bound
items.summary: A powerful sideways jump from one leg to the other, stuck on landing, for lateral power.

items.name: Skater Jump
items.summary: Rhythmic side-to-side single-leg jumps, like a speed skater's stride.

items.name: Pogo Hop
items.summary: Small, quick, continuous hops off the balls of the feet that train ankle stiffness and reactivity.

items.name: Hurdle Hop
items.summary: Consecutive two-footed jumps over a row of mini hurdles, keeping ground contact short.

items.name: Plyo Push-Up
items.summary: An explosive push-up where you push hard enough for your hands to leave the floor.

items.name: Clap Push-Up
items.summary: A plyo push-up with enough height to clap your hands before landing.

items.name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass
items.summary: An explosive two-handed throw from the chest into a wall or to a partner, using a medicine ball.

items.name: Medicine Ball Slam
items.summary: Lift a slam ball overhead and drive it hard into the floor, for full-body power and conditioning.

items.name: Medicine Ball Rotational Scoop Toss
items.summary: A low-to-high rotational throw into a wall that trains hip-driven rotational power.

items.name: Medicine Ball Rotational Side Throw
items.summary: A horizontal rotational throw at chest height into a wall, the classic rotational power drill for throwing and striking sports.

items.name: Medicine Ball Overhead Backward Throw
items.summary: A triple-extension throw that sends a medicine ball backward over your head for distance.

items.name: Snatch
items.summary: The Olympic lift that takes the bar from the floor to overhead in one movement, caught in a full overhead squat.

items.name: Power Snatch
items.summary: A snatch caught above parallel, demanding a higher, more powerful pull.

items.name: Hang Snatch
items.summary: A snatch started from a standing hang above the knees and caught in a full overhead squat.

items.name: Hang Power Snatch
items.summary: A snatch from the hang caught above parallel, a common way to train snatch speed and power.

items.name: Muscle Snatch
items.summary: A snatch with no re-bend of the knees: you pull and turn the bar over to overhead while standing tall.

items.name: Snatch Pull
items.summary: The snatch pull without the catch, used to build pulling strength and the finish position with heavier loads.

items.name: Overhead Squat
items.summary: A full squat with a barbell locked out overhead in a snatch grip, building the snatch receiving position.

items.name: Snatch Balance
items.summary: From the back rack, dip and drive yourself under the bar into an overhead squat, training speed under the snatch.

items.name: Dumbbell Snatch
items.summary: A one-arm snatch with a dumbbell from the floor to overhead in one explosive movement.

items.name: Clean
items.summary: The Olympic lift that takes the bar from the floor to the front of the shoulders, caught in a full front squat.

items.name: Power Clean
items.summary: A clean caught above parallel, the most common Olympic lift in strength and sports training.

items.name: Hang Clean
items.summary: A clean from a standing hang above the knees, caught in a full front squat.

items.name: Hang Power Clean
items.summary: A clean from the hang caught above parallel, a simpler entry to the clean for athletes.

items.name: Clean Pull
items.summary: The clean pull without the catch, for building pulling strength with loads heavier than your clean.

items.name: Barbell High Pull
items.summary: An explosive pull that continues past the shrug, driving the elbows high to bring the bar to chest height.

items.name: Push Press
items.summary: An overhead press driven by a quick leg dip, letting you move more weight than a strict press.

items.name: Push Jerk
items.summary: Dip and drive the bar off the shoulders, then drop into a partial squat to catch it locked out overhead.

items.name: Split Jerk
items.summary: The competition jerk: drive the bar overhead and split your feet to catch it, allowing the heaviest loads.

items.name: Clean and Jerk
items.summary: The full Olympic lift: clean the bar to your shoulders, stand, then jerk it overhead.

items.name: Kettlebell Swing
items.summary: The two-handed Russian swing: hinge and snap your hips forward to float the kettlebell to chest height.

items.name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Swing
items.summary: A kettlebell swing with one hand, adding an anti-rotation and grip challenge.

items.name: American Kettlebell Swing
items.summary: A kettlebell swing taken all the way to overhead, common in CrossFit.

items.name: Kettlebell Clean
items.summary: A hip-driven move that brings the kettlebell from between the legs to the rack position on your chest.

items.name: Kettlebell Snatch
items.summary: One explosive hip drive takes the kettlebell from between your legs to locked out overhead.

items.name: Turkish Get-Up
items.summary: A slow, step-by-step move from lying to standing with a kettlebell held overhead, training shoulder stability and the whole body.

items.name: Kettlebell Windmill
items.summary: With a kettlebell overhead, hinge sideways to reach the floor, training the obliques, hips and overhead stability.

items.name: Double Kettlebell Front Squat
items.summary: A squat holding two kettlebells in the rack position, which loads the legs and makes your core fight to stay upright.

items.name: Kettlebell Halo
items.summary: Circle a light kettlebell around your head to warm up and mobilise the shoulders and upper back.

items.name: Farmer's Walk
items.summary: Walk with a heavy weight in each hand to build grip, traps and a braced trunk; also done with kettlebells or farmer's handles.

items.name: Suitcase Carry
items.summary: Carry a heavy weight in one hand while staying perfectly upright, training the obliques and anti-lateral flexion.

items.name: Overhead Carry
items.summary: Walk with a kettlebell or dumbbell locked out overhead, for shoulder stability and core control; one-arm is often called a waiter's walk.

items.name: Front Rack Carry
items.summary: Walk with one or two kettlebells in the rack position, training the core to keep you upright.

items.name: Sandbag Bear Hug Carry
items.summary: Hug a heavy sandbag to your chest and walk, training the upper back, arms and core; needs a sandbag.

items.name: Keg Carry
items.summary: A strongman carry with a keg held against the chest; the shifting load trains grip, upper back and core.

items.name: Sled Push
items.summary: Drive a loaded sled across the floor with your legs, for leg power and conditioning with little muscle soreness.

items.name: Backward Sled Drag
items.summary: Walk backward pulling a sled by a strap or handles, a knee-friendly way to build the quads.

items.name: Hand-Over-Hand Sled Pull
items.summary: Stand still and pull a loaded sled toward you with a rope, hand over hand, for back and grip strength.

items.name: Sandbag Clean
items.summary: Lift a sandbag from the floor to your chest or shoulder with a powerful hip extension.

items.name: Tire Flip
items.summary: Lift and push a heavy tractor tire end over end, a full-body strongman event.

items.name: Yoke Walk
items.summary: Carry a heavy frame across your upper back for distance, building total-body strength and bracing.

items.name: Atlas Stone Load
items.summary: Lift a heavy round stone from the floor and load it onto a platform, the signature strongman event.

items.name: Log Press
items.summary: The strongman overhead press with a log and neutral grip, cleaned to the chest and pressed or push-pressed overhead.

items.name: Landmine Rotational Punch
items.summary: Push a landmine bar up and away from your shoulder with hip rotation, building punching power.

items.name: Band-Resisted Punch
items.summary: Throw punches against a band anchored behind you to train punching speed and endurance.

items.name: Sledgehammer Tire Strike
items.summary: Swing a sledgehammer overhead into a tire, for rotational and full-body power and conditioning.

items.name: Overhead Press
items.summary: The standing barbell press: the bar goes from the front of your shoulders to locked out overhead, training the delts, triceps and the whole trunk.

items.name: Seated Barbell Overhead Press
items.summary: A barbell press done seated on an upright bench, taking the legs and most of the balance out so the shoulders and triceps do the work.

items.name: Behind-the-Neck Press
items.summary: An overhead press that starts and finishes behind the head, putting more work on the side delts; only for lifters with excellent shoulder mobility.

items.name: Z Press
items.summary: A barbell press done sitting on the floor with legs straight out, which removes any leg drive or lean-back and demands a strong, upright trunk.

items.name: Landmine Press
items.summary: A single-arm press of a barbell anchored in a landmine, pressing up and forward on an arc that is friendly to stiff or sore shoulders.

items.name: Bradford Press
items.summary: A light barbell press that moves the bar from in front of the head to behind it and back, keeping the delts under constant tension.

items.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
items.summary: Pressing two dumbbells overhead from an upright bench, a staple for building the front and side delts.

items.name: Standing Dumbbell Shoulder Press
items.summary: A dumbbell press done standing, which adds core and balance work to the shoulder press.

items.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Shoulder Press
items.summary: A one-arm standing dumbbell press that trains each shoulder on its own and makes your trunk resist leaning to the side.

items.name: Arnold Press
items.summary: A seated dumbbell press that starts palms-in in front of the chest and rotates to palms-forward as you press, hitting the front and side delts through a long range.

items.name: Kettlebell Overhead Press
items.summary: A single-arm press from the kettlebell rack position, with the bell resting on the back of the forearm.

items.name: Kettlebell Bottoms-Up Press
items.summary: A press with the kettlebell held upside down, bell up, which demands a hard grip and steady rotator cuff control.

items.name: Machine Shoulder Press
items.summary: A seated press on a shoulder press machine, letting you push the delts hard without balancing a weight.

items.name: Smith Machine Shoulder Press
items.summary: A seated overhead press on a Smith machine, where the fixed bar path lets you focus on pushing hard with the delts.

items.name: Band Shoulder Press
items.summary: An overhead press against a resistance band anchored under your feet, a simple home or travel option that is hardest at the top.

items.name: Dumbbell Front Raise
items.summary: Raising dumbbells straight in front of you to shoulder height to isolate the front delts.

items.name: Cable Front Raise
items.summary: A front raise against a low cable, which keeps tension on the front delt through the whole range.

items.name: Barbell Front Raise
items.summary: A front raise with a barbell or EZ bar held in both hands, letting you load the front delts a little heavier.

items.name: Plate Front Raise
items.summary: A front raise holding a weight plate by its edges, a common finisher for the front delts.

items.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
items.summary: Raising dumbbells out to your sides to shoulder height, the go-to isolation exercise for the side delts.

items.name: Seated Dumbbell Lateral Raise
items.summary: A lateral raise done sitting on the end of a bench, which makes it much harder to swing the weight up.

items.name: Lean-Away Lateral Raise
items.summary: A one-arm lateral raise done while leaning away from a post, which shifts the hardest part toward the bottom of the lift.

items.name: Cable Lateral Raise
items.summary: A one-arm lateral raise from a low cable, giving the side delt steady tension from the very bottom of the rep.

items.name: Machine Lateral Raise
items.summary: A lateral raise on a dedicated machine with pads on the arms, a stable way to take the side delts close to failure.

items.name: Band Lateral Raise
items.summary: A lateral raise against a resistance band under your feet, which gets harder as your arms rise.

items.name: Cable Y-Raise
items.summary: Raising two low cables crossed in front of you up and out into a Y shape, working the side delts and lower traps together.

items.name: Bent-Over Reverse Fly
items.summary: Raising dumbbells out to the sides while bent over, the classic free-weight move for the rear delts.

items.name: Chest-Supported Reverse Fly
items.summary: A reverse fly lying face down on an incline bench, which takes your lower back out of it and stops you swinging the weight.

items.name: Cable Reverse Fly
items.summary: Pulling crossed cables apart at shoulder height, giving the rear delts constant tension through the whole range.

items.name: Reverse Pec Deck
items.summary: Sweeping the handles of a pec deck backward while facing the pad, a stable way to isolate the rear delts.

items.name: Face Pull
items.summary: Pulling a rope toward your face while rotating your hands outward, training the rear delts, rotator cuff and upper back for healthy shoulders.

items.name: Band Face Pull
items.summary: A face pull with a resistance band anchored at face height, an easy home version for the rear delts and rotator cuff.

items.name: Band Pull-Apart
items.summary: Stretching a band apart in front of your chest with straight arms, a simple warm-up and posture move for the rear delts and upper back.

items.name: Wide-Grip Upright Row
items.summary: Pulling a barbell up the front of your body with a wide grip, leading with the elbows, to work the side delts and upper traps.

items.name: Cable Upright Row
items.summary: An upright row with a bar or rope on a low pulley, giving smooth, constant tension on the side delts and traps.

items.name: Dumbbell Upright Row
items.summary: An upright row with a dumbbell in each hand, letting each arm follow its own path.

items.name: Band External Rotation
items.summary: Rotating your forearm outward against a band with your elbow at your side, a basic strengthener for the rotator cuff muscles that turn the arm out.

items.name: Band Internal Rotation
items.summary: Rotating your forearm inward across your body against a band, strengthening the rotator cuff muscles that turn the arm in.

items.name: Cable External Rotation
items.summary: An external rotation against a cable set at elbow height, with even resistance through the whole range for the rotator cuff.

items.name: Cable Internal Rotation
items.summary: An internal rotation against a cable at elbow height, strengthening the muscles that turn the arm inward.

items.name: Side-Lying External Rotation
items.summary: Lying on your side and rotating a light dumbbell upward with your elbow at your side, a classic physio exercise for the rotator cuff.

items.name: 90/90 External Rotation
items.summary: External rotation with your upper arm raised out to shoulder height and elbow at 90°, training the rotator cuff in the overhead position used for throwing and pressing.

items.name: Cuban Press
items.summary: A light dumbbell combo of an upright row, an external rotation and an overhead press, used to strengthen the rotator cuff and upper back.

items.name: Incline Y-T-W Raise
items.summary: Lying face down on an incline bench and raising light dumbbells in Y, T and W shapes, working the rear delts, rotator cuff and mid and lower traps.

items.name: Prone I-Y-T Raise
items.summary: Lying face down on the floor and lifting your arms in I, Y and T shapes, a no-equipment drill for the lower and mid traps and rear delts.

items.name: Wall Slide
items.summary: Sliding your arms up and down a wall with your back against it, training overhead reach and the serratus and lower traps that control your shoulder blades.

items.name: Pike Push-Up
items.summary: A push-up with your hips high in an inverted V, putting your shoulders in an overhead-press position with no equipment.

items.name: Feet-Elevated Pike Push-Up
items.summary: A pike push-up with your feet on a box or bench, putting more of your bodyweight on your shoulders as a step toward handstand push-ups.

items.name: Handstand Push-Up
items.summary: A full vertical press of your bodyweight from a handstand against a wall, one of the hardest bodyweight shoulder exercises.

items.name: Wall Walk
items.summary: Walking your feet up a wall and your hands in toward it until you're in a handstand, then walking back down, building shoulder strength and overhead confidence.

items.name: Wall Handstand Hold
items.summary: Holding a handstand with your chest or back against a wall, building the shoulder strength and body tension for handstand work.

items.name: Planche Lean
items.summary: Holding a straight-arm push-up position with your shoulders leaned well forward of your hands, the first step toward a planche.

items.name: Tuck Planche
items.summary: Balancing on straight arms with your knees tucked to your chest and your feet off the floor, an advanced calisthenics hold for the front delts.
